chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad narrated to me, saying: Abul Abbas al-Suraj narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Umar narrated to us, on the authority of Vaki’ah ibn al-Jarrah, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Khaythamah, on the authority of Abdullah, on the authority of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) who said:
It is not proper to stay awake and converse after the last night prayer (Isha) except for one of two people: one who is praying, or one who is traveling.

key_terms.سَمَرٌ: Late-night conversation or staying awake in discourse

ai.seo_question: Who are the two exceptions allowed to stay awake after Isha prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith in *Al-Khisal* to highlight the Prophetic etiquette of preserving health and spiritual readiness by limiting late-night socializing. The exception for the *musaalli* (one engaged in voluntary prayer) underscores the value of night worship (*Qiyam*), while the *musafir* (traveler) accounts for the practical necessity of travel preparations, reflecting a balanced approach to daily duties and devotion.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-125 Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad narrated that Abul Abbas al-Suraj quoted Abdullah ibn Umar, on the authority of Vaki’a ibn al-Jar’rah, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansoor (ibn al-Mua’tamar ibn Abdullah ibn Rabi’ah al-Kufy), on the authority of Khasamat (ibn Abdul Rahman), on the authority of Abdullah (ibn Mas’ood) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,
“It is not proper to stay awake after the night prayer except for two people: one who wants to pray, and one who is traveling.”
